title: Assessments filed under wrong subject/grade from Schoology source misassignment (Genius Challenge, Happy Healthy Me, Animal's Eyes unit test, HW Spiral Review, CFP Pre-Algebra Topic 1 / Topic 2 copy) — section, taker home-grade and standards all contradict the label
schools: Athenian Academy of Technology and the Arts
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED = TRUE, corrected affected_count = 12 (exact match). Rebuilt the detector from scratch (did not trust reported SQL). Independent item-level logic: within each section, flag items whose grade label is the minority (non-modal) grade, restricted to sections spanning >1 grade label; cross-check standards' modal grade token + section-sibling labels + twins.

VERIFIED:
- Exactly 8 sections span >1 grade label across all 3 schools (matches "8 sections"). One (7877376149 HS Algebra I, Higher-Ed vs Regular 9-12, both 912) is benign dual-band and correctly excluded.
- The 7 genuine mixed sections yield exactly 11 minority-grade outlier items; +1 Crestwell twin-mismatch (7841245375, single-item section) = 12 total.
- All 12 named item_ids exist with exactly the claimed filed subject/grade; each is a lone outlier inside an otherwise-unanimous section.

Standards vs filed grade (all contradict):
- Watkins 7337899755/74: filed ELA Grade1 -> 100% ELA.K (section unanimous Grade K).
- Burney 2nd 7628347421/7626433775: filed Grade5 -> 93.8-96.6% MA.6 (section Grade6).
- Burney 4th 7628391502/7626416439: filed Grade5 -> 93.2-100% MA.6/MA.7 (section Grade7).
- Swidarski 7892346412: filed ELA Grade8 -> 100% ELA.6, 39 students (section Grade6).
- MS PRE ALG 7964065626/7964067882: filed Math Grade7 -> 100% MA.8; siblings Topics 2-7 are Algebra/Grade8.
- Crestwell 7841245375: filed Math Grade2 -> 100% MA.1; two identical-content twins (7610639442/51) correctly filed Grade1.
- Genius Challenge 7616266129/7626085761: NO standards, but sit in a 22-item Science/Grade-1 section AND identical-title twins filed Science/Grade1 exist (7607478150, 7629339215, 7629339742); 18 students each.

'2 NEW' claim confirmed: Topic 1 / MS PRE ALG / Pre-Algebra item_ids are ABSENT from docs/audit/assessment_misfiling_audit.md and assessment_misfiling.csv; the other 10 appear there by name.

User-visible symptom confirmed at DB level: Topic 1 subject_id fad41a67... (dim_subject = Math/Grade 7) is shared by 4 items across 4 sections - 2 legit MS 07 MATH Topic 1 + the 2 misfiled MS PRE ALG Topic 1 - so Pre-Algebra Topic 1 pools into the real Grade-7 Math report while Topics 2-7 sit under Algebra/Grade 8.

'Still unfixed' confirmed: all 12 carry wrong labels in fact AND dim_item->dim_subject.

NUANCE: the reported section-granularity SQL alone returns 23 rows, most benign (HS/Grade-8 Algebra using 912 standards; whole-section Civics/Grade8 w/ SS.7 and History/Grade7 w/ SS.8 where every item shares the label). The finding's stated per-item drilldown correctly narrows to the 12 real item-level outliers; I independently arrived at the same 12. Severity critical is justified. Evidence CSV: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/section-teacher-integrity.csv
refute_notes:
CONFIRMED, not refuted. I tried every benign explanation and all failed against independent evidence. All 12 items reproduce exactly (Athenian 9, CFP 2, Crestwell 1) and each is a mislabel confirmed by MULTIPLE independent signals, not a detector artifact.

KEY DISPROOFS OF BENIGN HYPOTHESES:
1) Fact + dim_item + dim_subject all agree on the WRONG label (each flagged item has its own subject_id whose dim_subject row carries the same wrong subject/grade), so the report slicer really will surface these under the wrong subject/grade. Not a bad-join/grain artifact.
2) Standards contradict the label AFTER excluding all-grade ELA.K12 tokens: Through an Animal's Eyes = 100% ELA.6 (filed Grade 8); both Topic 1 = 100% MA.8 (filed Math/Grade 7); Chapter 1 Test = 100% MA.1 (filed Grade 2); the 4 Spiral Reviews' dominant tokens (MA.6/MA.7 at 83-100%) match their sections' true grade, not the Grade-5 label.
3) Sibling-within-unit proof: 'Happy Healthy Me' Weeks 2 & 4 and the Module Assessment (same unit, same Watkins section) are filed Grade K, while only Weeks 1 & 3 are filed Grade 1 — 100% ELA.K standards, 19/19 students overlap the Grade-K roster. Inconsistent labeling of one identical unit cannot be design.
4) Topic 1 vs Topic 2-7: same MS PRE ALG sections, same instructor (James Ryan), ALL MA.8 standards; Topics 2-7 are Algebra/Grade 8, only Topic 1 is Math/Grade 7. No benign sequencing explanation.
5) Genius Challenge items (no standards): all 18 test-takers are a subset of the 21 Grade-1 Science students in Elizabeth Sedlak's Grade-1 Science section; the items ('Inherited Traits', 'Plant Needs') are Science topics filed Algebra/Grade 8. The 'absence of standards is not proof' caveat is overridden by student-roster + item-topic + section-consensus evidence.
6) Higher-Ed dual-enrollment / course-name-subject / Reading-vs-ELA override benign paths are all inapplicable — no flagged grade is 'Higher-Ed', and these are generic subjects mislabeled across grades within one course/section.

CLASSIFICATION = source-data-corruption (not pipeline-bug): grade/subject are carried as denormalized text straight from the Schoology export through staging→dims→facts; the pipeline does NOT derive grade from the standard token (verified in backend/app/transformations — no grade-from-standard logic). The mislabel was already present in the source folder/course assignment we loaded; our transformations faithfully mirror it. It is still a real, teacher-visible defect (critical: wrong data appears under a chosen subject/grade slicer; the Pre-Algebra course fragments across two subject+grade combos), but the fix is a relabel at load/override, not a transformation bug fix — matching the existing misfiling-relabel runbook. Evidence CSV (12 rows) at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/STI-1-refute.csv. The 2 NEW Topic 1 items are genuinely misfiled and were correctly not in the prior audit doc.
evidence_sql: WITH std AS (SELECT f.school_id,f.section_nid,f.grade AS label_grade,f.subject,split_part(f.standard,'.',2) AS tok FROM fact_student_submission f WHERE f.standard NOT IN ('','nan') AND split_part(f.standard,'.',2) IN ('K','1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8','912')), agg AS (SELECT school_id,section_nid,label_grade,subject,tok,count(*) n, sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY school_id,section_nid,label_grade,subject) tot FROM std GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5), modal AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (school_id,section_nid,label_grade,subject) *, round(100.0*n/tot,1) pct FROM agg ORDER BY school_id,section_nid,label_grade,subject,n DESC) SELECT * FROM modal WHERE replace(label_grade,'Grade ','') <> tok AND pct >= 60; -- plus per-item drilldown on the 8 sections whose fact rows span >1 grade
sample: 7616266129 Inherited Traits 'Genius Challenge' (Sedlak, filed Algebra/Grade 8, is Science/Grade 1); 7626085761 Plant Needs 'Genius Challenge' (Sedlak, same); 7337899755 + 7337899774 Happy Healthy Me Weekly Wk1/Wk3 (Watkins, filed ELA/Grade 1, is Grade K); 7628347421 + 7626433775 HW 12/10 + 12/9 Spiral Review (Burney 4th Period, filed Grade 5, section is Grade 6); 7628391502 + 7626416439 HW 12/10 + 12/9 Spiral Review (Burney 2nd Period, filed Grade 5, section is Grade 7); 7892346412 Through an Animal's Eyes Unit Test (Swidarski 2nd Period, filed ELA/Grade 8, is Grade 6); 7964065626 + 7964067882 Topic 1 (MS PRE ALG 3rd A / 6th B, filed Math/Grade 7 vs siblings Algebra/Grade 8); 7841245375 Chapter 1 Test Counting and Number Sense (Crestwell Instructor 1, filed Grade 2, is Grade 1)
user_visible_symptom: Teachers pick e.g. 'Algebra / Grade 8' and see a Grade-1 science quiz with Grade-1 students; conversely the real class report (e.g. Swidarski's Grade-6 ELA, the Pre-Algebra course view) is missing an assessment its students actually took; the Pre-Algebra course fragments across two subject+grade slicer combos so no single view shows all 7 Topics.
root_cause_hypothesis: Schoology SOURCE mis-assignment: subject/grade come from the export folder, which was set inconsistently versus the course/section the assessment was actually given in. Not introduced by our transformations. The 10 doc-known items sit in the pending fix buckets (Fatima-review / dim_item-gap); the 2 Topic 1 items were never flagged before.
fix_direction: Extend the existing misfiling relabel procedure (docs/audit/fixes/02_assessment_misfiling_prod_runbook.md pattern): relabel subject_id/subject/grade on fact + dim_item + dim_question_data + dim_subject for these 12 item_ids to the section-consistent values, then rebuild cubes. Add the 2 Topic 1 items to the misfiling audit list.

title: Single assessments split across two subject_id buckets by export drift (assessment_type flips, renames, whitespace, band/session vintage) — 1-3-student fragment reports, stranded students, cross-layer name contradictions
schools: Athenian Academy of Technology and the Arts
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED (independent SQL). Core claim exact: my query `SELECT school_id,item_id FROM fact_student_submission GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(DISTINCT subject_id)>1` returns exactly 17 item_ids = Athenian 13 + CFP 2 + Crestwell 2, identical to report.

All sub-claims verified with my own queries:
- 34 buckets (17x2), each item splits into exactly 2 subject_id buckets; main cohort 12-29 st vs fragment 1-3 st. Sample matches (7334677961 16v3, 7797146594 29v1, 8362776921 16v1, 8159775714 17v1, 7929054690 15v3, etc.).
- Cohort DISJOINT in 15/17 pairs (my array-overlap check) = exact match to reported "15/17". The 2 overlapping items (7687741861, 7929054690) split the SAME student's attempts across two assessment_type buckets.
- Variant types all present: assessment_type flap ('Lesson  Assessments'/'Assessments'/'Unit-Chap  Assessments'); whitespace-only variant on 7797146594 verified (len 18 'Lesson Assessments' 29st vs len 19 'Lesson  Assessments' 1st); item-rename 7334739781/8112622324/8159775714; grade-band CFP 8362776921 Regular 9-12 vs Higher-Ed; session Crestwell 7610639442 2024-25 'Chap Test' vs 2025-26 'Summative'.
- CUBE SPLIT CONFIRMED: item 7334677961's 16 questions split 14+2 across the two subject_id entries in cube_question_summary; neither report entry shows the full assessment.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED: file_name is 100% NULL (0 of 1,646,988 rows non-null across all 3 schools). Read backend/app/transformations/07_facts/fact_student_submission.sql:130-174 -- the latest_export CTE (line 173: `WHERE w.max_export_ts IS NULL OR w.export_ts=w.max_export_ts`) is a genuine no-op when file_name is NULL; the code comment (lines 152-154) explicitly says NULL-date rows "are kept in full". Each subject_id maps 1:1 to a (subject,assessment_type,grade,session,item_name) combo (0 subject_ids carry >1 combo in Athenian), so the pipeline mints a distinct subject_id per label variant -> distinct report bucket. All 34 buckets exist in dim_subject, so each fragment IS a live slicer entry (the harm).

ADDITIONAL FINDING (beyond report): 4 of the 17 fragment buckets are entirely absent from cube_question_summary -- their 1-student data is dropped from per-question reports completely (e.g. CFP 8159775714 fragment = 0 cube rows). The other 13 fragments appear as separate slicer entries splitting the assessment.

Severity: critical (teachers see partial cohorts, split question lists, or a silently-lost fragment cohort). corrected_affected_count = 17 (unchanged). Evidence CSV (34 rows, both buckets per item, with fact vs cube question counts + overlap flag): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/TS-1.csv
refute_notes:
DETECTOR REPRODUCES: exactly 17 item_ids carry >1 subject_id/grade/session/item_name in fact (Athenian 13, CFP 2, Crestwell 2). But the finding's CRITICAL claims are REFUTED, and the true nature is source-side, not our pipeline minting spurious splits.

ORIGIN = SOURCE, mirrored faithfully (not our transformation). The variant labels already exist DISTINCTLY in stg_student_submission (earliest typed layer straight from the CSV parse). assessment_type/subject/grade/session/section are PATH-DERIVED from the Schoology export folder tree (backend/app/jobs/parsers/student_submission.py:110-115 + file_path_parser.py), item_name comes from the CSV row. The whitespace variant 'Lesson  Assessments' vs 'Assessments' is two DIFFERENT source folders holding a re-export of the SAME item+section (7334677961: same Sec 3, same 19 students, two type-folders). subject_id = uuid_6(school_id,subject,assessment_type,grade,session,item_name) is the LEGACY notebook formula verbatim (dim_subject.sql header cites notebook line 913-915/1168; dim_item.sql cites §4.4). So we mirror source folder duplication exactly as legacy did — this is source-data-corruption (Schoology export duplication / cross-section assignment), not a pipeline bug. The NULL file_name (100% of rows, all 3 schools — a derived/parquet-load property per memory) makes latest_export a NO-OP BY DESIGN (fact_student_submission.sql:152-154 explicitly keeps NULL-file_name rows in full), so it cannot dedupe cross-folder re-exports here — but that is expected for this load path, not a defect introduced by the split logic.

CRITICAL SYMPTOM REFUTED — teachers do NOT see wrong/partial numbers. (a) The cube 'totals' CTE (cube_question_summary.sql:99-119) groups by (school_id,item_id,question_id) ONLY, NOT subject_id, so every question's grade_average is the FULL cohort: item 7334677961 all questions ÷19 (8/19,13/19,19/19...); Higher-Ed item 8362776921 all questions ÷17 (7/17,7.5/17,10/17) = the pooled 16 Regular + 1 Higher-Ed takers, NOT 16 or 1. (b) The 14+2 question 'split' the finding cites exists ONLY as a non-deterministic DISTINCT ON tiebreak in the cube f_meta CTE (line 321-325: DISTINCT ON (...identifier) with ORDER BY not including subject_id) — in FACT all 16 questions appear under BOTH subject_ids. (c) The report read path (cube_repository.py:194-205) filters by item_id IN (SELECT item_id FROM dim_item WHERE subject_id=:sid), NOT by subject_id at question grain — so reading via EITHER subject_id entry returns ALL 16 questions (verified: twin sid → 16 questions; canonical sid → 32 = its 2 items × 16). The 14+2 cube split is invisible to users. (d) dim_item assigns exactly ONE subject_id per item (all 17), so the assessment appears under a valid single report entry.

RESIDUAL REAL DEFECT (narrow, label-hygiene only, medium severity): dim_subject retains BOTH label variants as slicer entries; for 5/17 items the twin subject_id also maps to a dim_item row, so a DUPLICATE slicer entry is reachable (e.g. 7334677961 shows under both 'Assessments' and 'Lesson  Assessments' Assessment-Type slicer values) — but both open the full assessment with full-cohort numbers. For the other 11/17 the fragment sid has 0 dim_item rows (unreachable — no phantom report). BENIGN sub-cases: CFP 8362776921 Higher-Ed vs Regular 9–12 is documented in docs/audit/assessment_misfiling_audit.md:81 as legitimate CFP dual-enrollment ('treated as legitimate, not misfiled'); Crestwell cross-session 7610639442 is 1+1 students.

NET: not refuted (a real duplicate-slicer/label artifact exists and warrants the canonicalization fix the finding proposes), but severity is MEDIUM not critical — the alarming 'per-question averages on partial cohorts / neither report shows the full assessment' claim is factually wrong (numbers are full-cohort correct; both reachable entries show the full question list). Root cause is source folder/section duplication we faithfully mirror (source-data-corruption), amplified by an expected NULL-file_name no-op and a cosmetic dim_subject twin-label retention — not our pipeline fabricating splits. Evidence CSV: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/TS-1-twin-split-refutation.csv
evidence_sql: SELECT school_id,item_id FROM fact_student_submission GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(DISTINCT subject_id)>1 OR count(DISTINCT grade)>1 OR count(DISTINCT session)>1 OR count(DISTINCT item_name)>1;  -- then per-bucket: SELECT subject_id,assessment_type,grade,session,count(DISTINCT user_uid),count(DISTINCT question_id) FROM fact_student_submission WHERE item_id=... GROUP BY 1,2,3,4

user_visible_symptom: The same assessment appears as two report entries (different type/grade/session slicer values); the main report is missing 1-3 students, and the question list itself is split between the two entries (e.g. 14 questions in one report, the other 2 questions only visible in the twin), so per-question class averages are computed on partial cohorts.
root_cause_hypothesis: Source-side: Schoology re-exports of the same item landed in different course folders / with edited names, and every fact row in this DB has file_name NULL so the latest_export prune (fact_student_submission.sql:130-175, keyed on file_name timestamp) is a NO-OP — stale re-export rows survive under their own label combo. Our pipeline then mints a distinct subject_id per (subject,type,grade,session,item_name) combo, turning each label variant into a separate report bucket. The Topic 8 Higher-Ed remnant matches the known open latest_export-omits-grade cross-band bug.
fix_direction: Per-item canonicalization pass: for each (school_id,item_id) with >1 subject_id, collapse fragment rows into the majority bucket's subject_id/labels (same relabel/twin-merge pattern as docs/audit/fixes/02_assessment_misfiling_prod_runbook.md), then rebuild cubes. Longer-term: make the fact build enforce one label-set per item_id (majority or dim_item-driven vote) and include an export-ordering fallback when file_name is NULL.

title: Re-created/duplicate assessment twins (same test under two item_ids) double-count overlapping students with contradictory scores in merged reports and cube_user_summary
schools: Athenian Academy of Technology and the Arts
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED and CONFIRMED via my own queries; the finding UNDERSTATES scope. Evidence CSV: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/ts-2.csv (44 rows).

COUNT SEMANTICS: The finding's affected_count=3 = number of cited assessments; its "8 duplicated students" = students in those 3 cases. I reproduce both exactly, AND find the pattern is systemic. corrected_affected_count=44 = distinct students double-counted in cube_user_summary (Athenian 38, Crestwell 5, CFP 1) across 11 harmful twin GROUPS. (If you prefer the "assessments" metric like the original, it is 11 twin groups, not 3.)

CITED CASES — all 3 verified with independent SQL:
(1) Crestwell "Chapter 1 Test: Counting and Number Sense": 3 item_ids (7610639442,7610639551 Grade1 / 7841245375 Grade2 subject_id a2871d3..., corrupted assessment_type "2 sectionsAll Sections"); same 9 questions, identical text by question_no, DIFFERENT question_ids. 4 students in both Grade1 & Grade2 buckets: 136696876 (6/9 vs 7/9), 136696884 (6/9 vs 6/9), 136696902 (6/9 vs 9/9), 136697026 (9/15 Summative 2025-26 vs 5/9 2024-25). file_name NULL → latest-export prune never fires. Confirmed.
(2) Crestwell 7929054690 "What Makes Us Who We Are?: Week 2": single item_id split into Summative vs Weekly Test subject_id buckets; users 134955415 & 134955460 in both; q2163559031 = 1pt(Summative,6/10) vs 0pt(Weekly,5/10) at SAME latest_attempt 2025-08-29 10:21:20. Confirmed.
(3) Athenian 7687741861 "Chapter 12" Math/GK: split "Assessments" vs "Lesson  Assessments"; users 131770756 & 131861995 both buckets; q2109257749 = 0pt(export 2025-01-29) vs 1pt(export 2025-02-05), SAME first_access → stale export beside regrade. Confirmed.

ROOT CAUSE VERIFIED: file_name is NULL on all these rows, so the latest-export-wins prune (latest_export CTE in fact_student_submission.sql) cannot fire; both/all vintages persist into fact and cubes. Twins split by (a) different item_id + different question_ids (re-publish), (b) same item_id but 2 subject_ids (assessment_type folder split: Summative/Weekly, Assessments/Lesson Assessments), or (c) cross-grade Schoology course mis-assignment.

NEW / LARGER cases the finding missed (detector = identical question-text fingerprint + overlapping students in same subject+session rollup):
- ATHENIAN "Module 1 Test" (Math Grade 7, 2025-26): items 7893465110 vs 8020987135, SAME subject_id, 25 identical questions, 27 students in BOTH with contradictory scores (e.g. 110144462: 20 vs 24; 126606628: 18 vs 24), exported Sep5 vs Sep8-9. cube_user_summary shows 54 user-item rows for 27 real students = 2x headcount inflation in the Grade7 Math rollup. This single case dwarfs all 3 cited.
- Athenian "Unit 2 Benchmark Test: The Engineering Process" (Science G3): 5 students.
- Athenian singles: "Everyone Has a Story: Week 3" (ELA G2), "Module 7 Week 2 Vocabulary Quiz", "Module 5 Test", "Module 1 Week 1 Vocabulary" (1 each) + Chapter 12 (2).
- CFP "Module 2 Assessment: Come to Your Senses" (ELA G4, 2025-26): items 8088499478 vs 8092034736, 1 student.

SEVERITY: critical stands — teachers see inflated headcounts/grade-averages/YTD and a student both correct and incorrect on the same question depending on which report entry they open.

COVERAGE NOTE (benign subset ruled OUT of the 44): content-identical item pairs where students do NOT overlap (multi-section same-name assessments given to different cohorts) are NOT double-counts and were excluded. Also excluded: 302 Athenian cross-SESSION content twins (same test reused next year, user_uid reused across years) — those land in separate session rollups, benign for single-session report views; 15 students there could double-count only in an all-sessions view (latent, medium-risk hygiene). Note the alternate title's attribution of "Everyone Has a Story: Week 3"/"Farrell" to CFP is inaccurate — that assessment is Athenian ELA Grade 2.
refute_notes:
CONFIRMED, not refuted. I verified the duplication end-to-end (raw -> staging -> fact -> cube_user_summary) and ruled out every benign explanation.

BASE CLAIM VERIFIED. Running the finding's SQL on cube_user_summary reproduces exactly: the same students appear under two item_ids/grades with contradictory scores for one item_name. Confirmed at fact and cube layers.

BENIGN EXPLANATIONS RULED OUT:
1. Course-name subjects / Reading-vs-ELA: N/A - every genuine twin is within ONE subject (Math or Reading). subject is identical across the two buckets; only subject_id/grade/assessment_type differ.
2. Dual-enrollment: RULED OUT for the flagged cases. The 4 Crestwell 'Chapter 1' students appear in the Grade-2 course (7696815268) for EXACTLY ONE item (the corrupted 'stub2 sectionsAll Sections' twin); their entire real curriculum is the Grade-1 'Math 1st' course (7554585430). A real dual-enrollee would appear across many Grade-2 items. 'stub2 sectionsAll Sections' is a one-off corrupt assessment_type - only 1 item in the entire 1.65M-row dataset has it.
3. Legitimate multi-section splits: RULED OUT. Per-question rows show the SAME student, SAME question_id, SAME timestamp with DIFFERENT answer text and DIFFERENT scores (Crestwell Week2 q2163559031: correct 'b...' 1pt in Summative vs wrong 'a...' 0pt in Weekly Test, both at 2025-08-29 10:21:20). A single event cannot have two answers.
4. Cross-year retest (the big false-positive class): EXCLUDED. A naive item_name detector flags 3107 Athenian 'twins' but ~all are cross-SESSION (same test next school year = legitimate). Restricting to same-session collapses to 2 Athenian users / 1 item.
5. CFP name-collision (my detector surfaced 20 CFP 'twins' the finding omitted): these ARE benign and I excluded them. 'Topic 2'/'Topic 3' etc. are generic names colliding across genuinely different courses; item 8089937013 (HS Algebra II: functions/projectile questions) vs 8261346599 (HS Economics: society's economic goals) have DIFFERENT question content and different item_ids - a dual-enrolled Higher-Ed student legitimately took both. Not a double-count.
6. Detector error: RULED OUT - reproduced at raw, staging, fact, and cube layers with matching answer text.

TRUE SCOPE (after excluding benign): 3 assessments, 8 duplicated students - Crestwell 'Chapter 1 Test: Counting and Number Sense' (4 users, cross-grade Grade1+Grade2, cross-item 7610639442/7610639551 vs 7841245375), Crestwell 'What Makes Us Who We Are?: Week 2' item 7929054690 (2 users, Summative vs Weekly Test), Athenian 'Chapter 12' item 7687741861 (2 users, Assessments vs 'stubLesson  Assessments'). Matches the finding's count exactly.

CLASSIFICATION = pipeline-bug (mechanism confirmed in code + data): The legacy backup accumulating re-exports/regrades is source behavior, but our transformation is responsible for failing to dedupe it, so the same event reaches the report cube TWICE with contradictory numbers teachers see. Two distinct failure modes proven:
(a) Crestwell: parquet-direct-loaded 2024-25 rows have EMPTY file_name in fact. The latest_export CTE (fact_student_submission.sql:159-174) parses export_ts from file_name; NULL -> max_export_ts NULL -> WHERE clause keeps ALL rows (comment lines 152-154 admit this). Prune never fires.
(b) Athenian: file_name IS present with parseable dates in STAGING (Chapter-12-2025-01-30 vs 2025-02-11), so the prune should pick the newer export. But the latest_export PARTITION BY (line 160-161) includes `submission`, and each re-export increments the submission counter (verified: same question_id 2109257749, same answer 'b. 2', submission=1 in the Jan export vs submission=2 in the Feb export). Different submission -> different partition -> a separate max_export_ts per submission value -> BOTH vintages survive. The prune's grain is too fine to catch re-exports that bump the submission counter. Additionally file_name is dropped entirely from the fact table (present in stg, blank in fact), so no downstream recovery is possible.

Net: real double-count, teacher-visible contradictory scores, critical severity. Fix is a targeted twin merge per runbook plus tightening latest_export (drop `submission` from the prune partition, or add a same-content/same-latest_attempt collapse) and preserving file_name into fact. title: Same-name merge keyed on (subject_id, question_no) pools genuinely different question content — recycled quiz titles ('Quarter 3 Quiz 2', 'Quiz 2/3') and 302 mixed-question slots across 68 merged assessments

repro_notes:
REPRODUCED (302 unchanged; 121 Athenian + 122 CFP + 59 Crestwell across 68 subject_ids = 37+19+12). Wrote my own independent detector rather than trusting the reported SQL: distinct normalized (HTML-stripped, alphanumeric-only, lowercased) question text PER item, then required text disagreement genuinely ACROSS different item_ids within one (school, subject_id, question_no) grain over non-empty text. Got exactly 302 grains / 68 subjects, identical to reported.

Merge design confirmed in code: backend/app/repositories/cube_repository.py pools all items sharing a subject_id (item_id IN (SELECT item_id FROM dim_item WHERE subject_id=:subject_id)) and GROUPs per-question numerics BY question_no (lines ~280-285 and ~663-670). So different questions under one question_no do blend. cube_question_summary.sql itself is keyed by item_id/question_id and is NOT the defect; the report-layer merge is.

Fact-level smoking gun: Athenian subject 5a9fa1a8… 'Quiz 2' Q4 pools item 8126292235 (qid 2213766973, 'Which of the following banned trade with just England…', 24 students @83.3%) with item 8257448535 (qid 2249531491, 'Ulysses S. Grant had the nickname…', 23 students @95.7%) — one 'Question 4' row blends 47 students' scores from two unrelated questions.

Denominator/ratio confirmed: 18,949 total merged question grains, 302 conflicts = 1.59% (matches reported ~1.6%).

Confounders I ruled out (reported SQL didn't): (1) multi-text is NOT a within-item standards-fanout artifact — all 302 differ across distinct items. (2) One cited sample is WRONG: CFP 9d5572b5… 'Amazing Animals' Q3 collapses to n_texts=1 under normalization (identical text, whitespace-only differences) and is correctly excluded from the flagged set — the reported detector handles it right, only the prose example was bad.

Precision of the 302: 237 differ within the first 25 normalized chars (unambiguously different questions); 65 share a 25-char stem and differ later (same-passage/different-subpart reading items plus a few trivial 'box 1' vs 'blank' phrasing variants). Even conservatively 237 are real different-question conflicts. Severity high is justified (teachers see one question's text with statistics blended from an unrelated question). Root cause per finding is correct: generic recycled titles (e.g. History 'Quiz 2', 'Chapter 5') reused across sections/dates share assessment name + subject_id while carrying different question content; the merge assumes question_no => same question.

refute_notes:
PARTIALLY REFUTED — the finding is a mixture; its headline count (302 grains) overcounts by ~2/3 due to a detector counting artifact, but a genuine ~102-grain core survives as a real pipeline bug.

REPRODUCTION: The detector SQL reproduces exactly (Athenian 121, CFP 122, Crestwell 59 = 302 grains, 68 subjects). The merge mechanism is real and confirmed in code: cube_repository.py:649-670 picks ONE representative question text per question_no via DISTINCT ON while SUM-pooling points across every section's question_id sharing that question_no; base cube_question_summary.sql grains on (item_id,question_id,position,identifier) so pooling occurs only in the report merge, keyed on (subject_id,question_no) exactly as claimed.

ARTIFACT PORTION (200/302 grains, 55 subjects) — DETECTOR ERROR: I split the 302 grains by a truncation-independent discriminator — whether the colliding items share an IDENTICAL question_no set (=same assessment given to multiple sections). 55/68 subjects (200 grains) are structurally identical assessments. The n_texts>1 flag here is spurious: the `question` field embeds the full reading passage inline (capped at 7500 chars) and different section exports embed different amounts of passage vs bare stem. Proven on CFP subject 29ec9808 'Module 2 Assessment: What a Story' (ELA G5, same date 2025-10-22, sections 05 LA-A/B): both items have 29 identical question_no AND 29 question_id; at Q20/Q22 both carry the byte-identical stem ('synonym for construct?', 'How are crocodiles and alligators DIFFERENT?'), section A merely prepends the passage. Item A had 50 dqd rows but only 13 distinct normalized texts because 29 were capped at 7500 chars. The alphanumeric-normalized comparison sees 'passage+stem' vs 'stem' and declares them different. Corroboration: 124/302 grains share the same correct_answer across items; 83/302 the shorter text is an exact substring of the longer.

GENUINE PORTION (102/302 grains, 13 subjects) — REAL pipeline bug: These have structurally DIFFERENT assessments (differing question counts 5-vs-10, 5-vs-19, 9-vs-13) sharing a generic recurring name. Verified on Athenian subject 5a9fa1a8 'Quiz 2' (History G7): item 8126292235 = 5-question War-of-1812 quiz (2025-11-14), item 8257448535 = 10-question Civil-War quiz (2026-02-13), SAME section (5th Period) / SAME instructor (Hitzig), 3 months apart. The merge pools both Q4s (item A 'banned trade with England' + item B 'Grant nickname') into one report row at a blended 89.4% — I confirmed cube_question_summary pools 2 items/2 question_ids into question_no=4. The user-visible symptom (one text, blended stats from an unrelated question) is real for these. The 13 genuine subjects are dominated by generic names: 'Quiz 2/3', 'Topic 1/2', 'HW 12/9 Spiral Review', '7.2 Grammar Review', 'Chapter 1 Test'.

CLASSIFICATION: pipeline-bug, not source-data-corruption or benign-by-design. The genuine root cause is NOT the detector's hypothesis ('sections got different question variants'); it is that OUR merge key subject_id = uuid_6(School,Subject,Assessment_type,Grade,Session,Item_Name) collapses on item_name, so two distinct assessments with an identical generic name (e.g. two 'Quiz 2's) receive the same subject_id and get merged, pooling unrelated questions under one question_no. Benign source naming (recurring generic names) triggers a defect introduced by our merge design (a known limitation of project_merge_section_reports). The fix_direction is sound but the affected_count should be ~102 grains / 13 subjects (not 302 / 68); severity is closer to medium than high given the artifact-inflated count and that the guard should key on structural assessment identity, not merely n_texts>1 (which would wrongly exclude the 55 same-assessment multi-section subjects that SHOULD merge). Full per-grain classification written to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/QSA-5.csv (302 rows). title: 29 dim_subject buckets holding 7,730 fact rows plus cube rollups have no dim_item row (26 twin-split orphan sides + 3 CFP no-twin orphans) — unreachable from every report item list
schools: Athenian Academy of Technology and the Arts
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED from scratch with independently-written queries. Core claim fully confirmed.

Counts matched to the digit:
- 29 dim_subject rows have NO dim_item referencing their (school_id, subject_id): Athenian 25, CFP 3, Crestwell 1.
- Fact rows under them: 7,730 total (Athenian 7,285 / CFP 305 / Crestwell 140), via both the finding's NOT-EXISTS query and an explicit JOIN to the 29 orphan rows.
- Distinct students: 283 total (238/30/15; no cross-school overlap).
- All 29 have cube_school_summary AND cube_question_summary rows (29/29) but ZERO dim_item rows (0/29) — confirming they roll up into school-level cubes yet are unreachable from item enumeration.
- 26/29 have a label-twin (same subject/grade/session/item_name, different subject_id) that HAS dim_item rows; all 26 twins differ specifically by assessment_type (e.g. 'Lesson  Assessments' vs 'Assessments'). Matches the '26 split assessments' alternate framing.
- 3/29 have no twin, all CFP: the HS Algebra I / Higher-Ed / 'Topic 8' cross-band remnant (subject_id 38fa194a..., 1 stu / 33 rows) plus 2 CFP ELA Grade 4 2025-26 Summative weekly assessments. Matches '3 CFP rows with no dim_item and no twin'.

Code claim VERIFIED: cube_repository.py:377 scoped_items CTE selects FROM dim_item di (dashboard assessment list), and the report item-set CTE 'SELECT item_id FROM dim_item WHERE subject_id = :subject_id' appears at 20+ sites (194, 510, 642, 781, 858, 934, 1205, 1312, ...). A dim_subject with no dim_item yields an empty item set, so these subjects can never be listed or opened -> genuine data-loss/unreachability.

Ruled out a benign explanation: show_history_subject carries the subject LABEL (not a boolean hide flag) and is populated on all rows, so these are not intentionally hidden.

Minor narrative imprecisions in the finding text (do NOT affect the count): (1) the single Crestwell orphan is 2025-26 Summative with an assessment_type twin, not a '2024-25 session twin' as loosely stated; (2) '24 of 29 assessment-type twins' is conservative — all 26 label-twins differ by assessment_type.

Key query I ran:
WITH orphan AS (SELECT s.* FROM dim_subject s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dim_item i WHERE i.school_id=s.school_id AND i.subject_id=s.subject_id)) SELECT sc.school_name, count(*) orphans, sum over fact rows / distinct user_uid via JOIN to fact_student_submission.

STRUCTURAL CLAIM CONFIRMED, IMPACT CLAIM REFUTED. The query reproduces exactly (Athenian 25 + CFP 3 + Crestwell 1 = 29 orphan dim_subject rows; 7,285/305/140 fact rows). But the finding's severity-driving claims ("unreachable", "silently absent", "~283 students of data lost", "high") are wrong.

Reachability disproved: all 29 orphan item_ids DO exist in dim_item — under a DIFFERENT (twin) subject_id, not zero rows (verified: every orphan item resolves to 'dim_item exists but DIFFERENT subject_id'). 100% of the 29 items appear in cube_question_summary (scored) and cube_school_summary (headcounts): bool_and(reachable)=t, bool_and(scored)=t over 29/29. Reports/dashboard enumerate items and read scores by ITEM_ID (cube_repository.py scoped_items CTE + item_ga '... WHERE item_id IN (SELECT item_id FROM scoped_items)'; report items-CTE 'SELECT item_id FROM dim_item WHERE subject_id=:subject_id' opened under the twin subject). Simulating the live dashboard query, the orphan items render under the twin: e.g. Athenian Math/G5 'Chapter 12' shows grade_average 0.847 / 19 students; fact students (20) == cube students (20) for that item_id — no student or score data is lost. The orphan dim_subject ROW is an unreachable duplicate LABEL, not a data-loss channel.

Root cause is a real pipeline defect (so NOT benign-by-design, refuted=false): dim_item.sql builds one row per (school_id,item_id) via SELECT DISTINCT ON (school_id,item_id) ORDER BY assessment_date ASC. When one item_id carries multiple subject_ids in staging, dim_item keeps the EARLIEST while fact (multi-export latest-wins) settles on the LATEST export's subject_id, orphaning the fact-side subject. This is the same mechanism as RO-1; the transformation — not just the source — produces the orphan dim_subject and the category-label mismatch.

The TRIGGER is source-data inconsistency: staging carries the same item_id under two assessment_type spellings (item 7594902377: 'Lesson  Assessments' 942 rows vs 'Assessments' 496 rows) — Schoology export noise. Twin-cause tally: 26/29 assessment_type variants (mostly whitespace/prefix, e.g. 'Lesson  Assessments' vs 'Assessments'), 2 item_name variants (date-suffix/reword), 1 genuine grade-band split (CFP HS Algebra I 'Topic 8' Higher-Ed = a single student's Algebra assessment mis-assigned in Schoology to a US-History section 'Sec HS US HIST - 4th'; 1 student, 387 rows). None of the offered benign explanations (course-name subjects, Reading-vs-ELA, dual-enrollment Higher-Ed) apply: subject/grade/session are identical across 25 of the twins — the split is purely assessment_type-string noise.

Classified pipeline-bug because the orphan dim_subject rows and the user-visible symptom (a few assessments filed under a slightly different assessment_type CATEGORY label than their fact rows indicate — e.g. under 'Assessments' instead of 'Lesson  Assessments') are produced by dim_item's DISTINCT-ON first-occurrence pick, not present as-such in the source. Actual severity is medium (label/hygiene + latent cube/dim_item subject_id divergence), NOT high — no scores or students are missing from any report. Fix: normalize assessment_type whitespace/prefix before hashing subject_id, then regenerate dim_item.subject_id from the deduped fact (or merge the twin dim_subject rows per the misfiling runbook); afterwards the orphan query returns 0. title: dim_item keeps the FIRST-occurrence bucket while fact keeps the LATEST-export bucket — 37 items diverge on subject_id (12 pointing at minority fragments, 20 at zero-fact buckets) with no deterministic tiebreak so rebuilds can flip

repro_notes:

- 37 items where dim_item.subject_id disagrees with fact.subject_id: 32 Athenian + 3 CFP + 2 Crestwell. Confirmed by TWO independent methods (cube_question_summary join AND direct fact join) — both yield 32/3/2 = 37.

- fact_student_submission.sql:130-174 latest_export CTE prunes to newest export per response slot; fact subject_id uses the SAME uuid_6 formula (lines 327-329). Two independent 'pick one bucket' rules -> systematic disagreement. Root cause hypothesis is sound.
- cube_repository.py uses `item_id IN (SELECT item_id FROM dim_item WHERE subject_id = :subject_id)` in 20+ read paths (MORE than cited '12+': lines 194,510,642,781,858,934,1205,1312,1865,1912,2151,2496,2606,2639,2653,2710,2724,2790,2891,2964,3006).

Both slicer entries can render empty question tables. All 20 orphaned items have BOTH buckets present in dim_subject (both slicer entries appear).

refute_notes:

MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN CODE: dim_item.sql (03_dimensions_b/dim_item.sql:69-107) computes subject_id=uuid_6(school_id,subject,assessment_type,grade,session,item_name) and keeps the FIRST occurrence by ROW_NUMBER ORDER BY assessment_date ASC — NO latest_export pruning. fact_student_submission.sql (07_facts/:130-175) computes the identical uuid_6 but FIRST applies the latest_export CTE (keeps only newest-export rows per response slot) THEN computes subject_id. Verified causally: 33/37 fact buckets equal the item's NEWEST-export assessment_type; dim_item picks a stale export's bucket.

Weekly Assessment: Week 1' — staging carries BOTH 'Lesson Assessments' (324 rows, export 2025-01-27) and 'Assessments' (342 rows, export 2025-01-30). Latest_export keeps 2025-01-30 -> all fact+cube rows under ELA|Assessments|Grade 1 (subject f858...). dim_item picks ELA|Lesson Assessments|Grade 1 (subject ade6...), which has ZERO fact rows. (2) Faithful legacy mirroring — NO; legacy ran incrementally so newest export reached both fact and dim consistently, whereas our full-rebuild dim_item.sql omits the latest_export prune the fact applies, so the two tables systematically pick opposite buckets — the divergence is introduced by our transformation asymmetry. (3) Same-name multi-section merge — NO; merge is keyed on subject_id and all 37 pairs have DIFFERENT subject_ids, so they cannot union. (4) Course-name/Reading-override/Higher-Ed/K12 benign designs — irrelevant; subject and grade are identical in 32/37, only assessment_type folder differs.

Although the underlying source ambiguity (same item in two assessment-type/name folders across re-exports) originates in Schoology, the specific defect — dim_item.subject_id disagreeing with fact and breaking 23 read paths — is created by our own transformation logic (dim_item not applying the fact's latest_export window before its first-occurrence dedupe). Fix direction is correct: rebuild dim_item.subject_id from the post-latest_export surviving rows (or apply the same latest_export window in dim_item.sql), then verify every dim_item.subject_id has fact rows. Meanwhile fact_dedup (lines 2311-2313) filters `fss.subject = :subject`, which DOES match (fact_student_submission carries the override label), so the fact side returns rows -> single pooled 'Other' column.

- fact_student_submission has 3,772 rows subject='HS Physics' (pp>0); dim_question_data has 0 rows q.subject='HS Physics' (via dim_item school); 250 rows reachable via dim_subject join, all carrying base label 'Science' (235 with standards). title: Superseded retake attempts retained in fact and consumed non-deterministically: three read paths DISTINCT ON without ORDER BY submission DESC, and 684 (user,item) scores differ from latest-attempt semantics
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED (critical, pipeline-logic). Wrote my own queries; did not trust the reported SQL.

CODE VERIFIED (read both files):
- cube_repository.py:207-215 get_canonical_kpis_for_item -> ORDER BY user_uid, question_id, position_number, identifier NULLS LAST (NO submission DESC).
- cube_repository.py:521-529 get_canonical_per_question_grades -> same, identifier NULLS LAST only (NO submission DESC).
- cube_repository.py:2300-2317 get_ytd_longitudinal_cells -> ORDER BY ..., fss.standard NULLS LAST (NO submission DESC).
- student_repository.py:95-104 per-student report -> ORDER BY ..., f.submission DESC NULLS LAST, f.identifier NULLS LAST (CORRECT/immune).
- cube_repository.py:2528-2542 QSR per_attempt -> ORDER BY ..., fss.submission DESC NULLS LAST, fss.latest_attempt DESC NULLS LAST (CORRECT/immune).
So 3 read paths dedupe fact rows without the submission DESC tiebreaker while 2 paths do it correctly -> same student+assessment can show different scores across pages. Confirmed.

DATA VERIFIED (my queries):
- evidence_sql reproduced to the digit: 5,750 divergent (user,item,question,position) clusters (n_att>1 AND n_pts>1): Athenian 814 clusters/30 items/117 students, CFP 4,324/127/213, Crestwell 612/37/69.
- affected_count = 990 distinct (user,item) pairs (192 Athenian + 670 CFP + 128 Crestwell) -> matches exactly, keeping 990 as corrected count.
- Item score actually FLIPS between latest-attempt and earliest-attempt dedup on 921 (user,item) pairs (186+612+123) -- the true user-visible blast radius; 990 is the superset (clusters with divergent points that may net to same item total).
- Sample student Ariah Lazri, Athenian item 8193578592 'World History Quiz 1': attempt1=0 pts/q, attempt2=1 pt/q; item = 100% under latest vs 20% under attempt-1 pick. Direction/mechanism matches finding.
- Top affected assessments match finding's samples (U.S. History Quiz 2 = 19 students, CFP Test Topic 2 Fertile Crescent = 18, World History Quiz 1 = 17, etc.).

STRENGTHENING NUANCE I proved: in 4,811/5,750 divergent clusters the `identifier` is CONSTANT across attempts, so the wrong path's `identifier NULLS LAST` tiebreaker cannot distinguish attempts at all -> pick is fully plan/heap-order arbitrary. In the 939 clusters where identifier varies, the identifier-ordered pick still disagrees with the latest attempt in 453 cases. So the wrong-ordered paths never reliably select the latest attempt.

MINOR CODE INACCURACY (non-blocking): QSR comment cube_repository.py:2524 says fss.submission is UUID v7; column is actually integer (1,2,...). submission DESC ordering is still correct (higher int = later attempt), so no behavior bug -- just a wrong comment.

Fix direction confirmed sound: add f.submission DESC NULLS LAST before identifier/standard in the DISTINCT ON ORDER BY at cube_repository.py:215, :529, :2317, mirroring student_repository.py:104.

Evidence CSV (990 rows, worst-case latest-vs-earliest swing per user-item): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/score-sanity-1.csv
refute_notes:
REFUTATION FAILS — finding CONFIRMED as a real pipeline bug in OUR read layer. Every benign explanation was ruled out with direct queries.

CODE (verified by reading the files):
- Three cited paths dedupe with DISTINCT ON but omit submission DESC: cube_repository.py get_canonical_kpis_for_item (ORDER BY ...position_number, identifier NULLS LAST, ~L215), get_canonical_per_question_grades (~L529), get_ytd_longitudinal_cells (ORDER BY ...position_number, standard NULLS LAST, ~L2316-2317).
- Sibling paths correctly use submission DESC NULLS LAST: student_repository.py:104 and the QSR per_attempt CTE cube_repository.py:2539-2540. So the same student+assessment can show different scores on different pages. Not detector error.

DATA:
- submission is an INTEGER attempt counter (1,2,...), higher = later attempt (the QSR comment claiming it is UUIDv7 is factually wrong but harmless). So submission is exactly the discriminator the buggy paths drop.
- Cluster counts reproduce the finding exactly: Athenian 814, CFP 4324, Crestwell 612 clusters (n_att>1 AND n_pts>1), 5750 total; 990 user-items.
- Non-determinism is real: in 4815/5750 multi-attempt clusters the identifier tiebreak does NOT distinguish attempts (305 fully blank), so Postgres DISTINCT ON picks an ARBITRARY attempt. In the 935 clusters where identifier does differ, identifier-ascending picks the NON-latest attempt in 497 and yields wrong points in 480.
- Verified end-to-end on real Athenian item 8193578592 'World History Quiz 1': buggy per-question path returns Q1=42.1% vs correct latest-attempt 73.7% (31.6-pt error), plus 4 more questions diverging 2.6-18.4 pts. Ariah Lazri concretely has attempt1=0/1 and attempt2=1/1 per question with a BLANK identifier and identical latest_attempt timestamp — a textbook arbitrary-pick.
- All three paths are LIVE: called from report_service.py:328 (dashboard KPIs), :513/:1825 (per-question tables), :882 (YTD matrix).

CLASSIFICATION: pipeline-bug. Keeping every attempt in fact_student_submission is by design (legacy latest-attempt semantics); the defect is entirely in our read-layer dedupe ordering, introduced by the earlier canonical-KPI determinism fix that added identifier ordering (which does not distinguish attempts). The fix (add f.submission DESC NULLS LAST before identifier/standard at the three DISTINCT ON blocks) mirrors the already-correct student_repository/QSR paths.

Caveat: submission DESC and latest_attempt DESC disagree on 'latest' in 4016/7910 multi-attempt clusters, so the fix should follow the established codebase convention (submission DESC, as in student_repository.py:104 and QSR) rather than latest_attempt, to stay consistent with the canonical latest-attempt grain. Evidence CSV (5750 flagged clusters): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/score-sanity-1.csv

root_cause_hypothesis: Our transformation keeps every Schoology attempt in the fact (by design), but the read-layer canonical dedupe was written without the submission DESC tiebreaker in these three queries (the earlier canonical-KPI determinism fix only added identifier ordering, which does not distinguish attempts). Introduced by our code, not the source.
fix_direction: Add `f.submission DESC NULLS LAST` (before identifier/standard) to the DISTINCT ON ORDER BY at cube_repository.py:208, :522 and :2303, mirroring student_repository.py:95-104. Add a regression test with a 2-attempt fixture.

title: Duplicate dim_standard identifiers from ILIKE prefix collision (44 codes with 2 identifiers/descriptions) — fact pins the wrong benchmark for 18,220 rows and cube builds tie-break nondeterministically, showing different descriptions per school and flipping labels on rebuild
schools: Athenian Academy of Technology and the Arts
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED — core claim fully confirmed with my own independent queries (I did not trust the finding's regex; I re-derived using a last-token match and got identical numbers). Evidence CSV: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/SCG-1.csv (all 44 ambiguous codes, pinned vs correct identifier/description, per-code fact exposure).

CONFIRMED NUMBERS (my SQL):
- dim_standard: EXACTLY 44 schoology_standard codes map to >1 identifier; all 44 also have >1 distinct description; 9 also have >1 distinct strand label. Matches finding exactly.
- Prefix-collision proven: identifier c2a1b207 (canonical W.3.1 'Phoenicians', standard_new=1) is attached to 9 distinct codes (SOC.6.SS.6.W.3.1, .3.10-.3.16, SS.6.W.3.1). cbd1b207→7 codes (SS.8.A.3.x), ccd1b207→6 codes (SS.8.A.4.x). Classic ILIKE substring collision (W.3.1 substring-matches W.3.10-16).
- fact pipeline logic CONFIRMED by reading backend/app/transformations/07_facts/fact_student_submission.sql lines 223-231: LATERAL join `SELECT identifier FROM dim_standard WHERE schoology_standard = qd.standard ORDER BY identifier LIMIT 1` — pins the lexically-smallest identifier per code. The code comment (lines 215-222) even acknowledges the CSV pollution but treats the lex-min pin as acceptable.
- Mis-pinned count: 23 of 35 referenced ambiguous codes have the wrong pinned identifier (pinned standard_new != code last token), = 18,220 fact rows. IDENTICAL to finding. 12 codes pin correctly (7,638 rows). Total exposure of all 44 ambiguous codes: 25,858 fact rows / 162 items / 851 students — matches finding exactly.
- Per-school breakdown EXACT match: Athenian 16,252 rows / 21 codes / 71 items; CFP 1,634 / 14 / 24; Crestwell 334 / 4 / 6.
- Downstream symptom verified: 4 distinct benchmarks (W.3.10/.12/.13/.14) all carry the single wrong identifier c2a1b207 in fact, so standards reports credit them to the W.3.1 'Phoenicians' benchmark (wrong description) and pool distinct benchmarks.

SECONDARY findings (also reproduced):
- cube_question_summary_overall nondeterministic description: EXACTLY 11 ambiguous codes carry 2 distinct descriptions in the live cube today (matches '11 codes affected'). Root cause confirmed in cube_question_summary_overall.sql lines 212/227: `DISTINCT ON (long_standard) ... ORDER BY long_standard, schoology_standard` has no effective tiebreak (schoology_standard = long_standard), so the description pick is arbitrary; the comment 'their descriptions are expected to match anyway' is false.
- cube_overallperformance_summary non-deterministic standards label: mechanism confirmed in cube_overallperformance_summary.sql lines 51-55 (`DISTINCT ON (school_id, question_id) ... ORDER BY ... identifier NULLS LAST`, no tiebreak on standards). My count of tie-affected questions = 403 (finding said 424 — same mechanism, count off by ~5% likely due to data vintage or a slightly different tie definition; still ~400 questions can flip label on rebuild).

CORRECTED affected_count: 18,220 (fact rows mis-attributed to the wrong benchmark) — same as reported. Severity critical is appropriate: teachers see the wrong standard description and pooled/wrong per-standard averages in standards reports, and distinct benchmarks collapse into one cube_standard_summary row.

Minor note: the only per-code characterization nuance is MA.912.AR.3.1 — the finding lists it as a mismatch example, but its fact pin actually lands on the CORRECT segment (std_new=1); the divergence there is the alias-description tie-break in the cube, not the fact pin. This does not change any aggregate count.
refute_notes:
CONFIRMED, NOT REFUTED. I reproduced every headline number and traced the defect end-to-end, and every benign explanation failed.

REPRODUCTION (exact): dim_standard has exactly 44 schoology_standard codes carrying 2 distinct identifiers each (max=2). The finding's evidence_sql reproduces to the digit: 23 code/identifier pairs where the pinned identifier's standard_new != the code's trailing segment = 18,220 fact rows; 12 pairs where it matches = 7,638; total 25,858 rows / 162 items / 851 students. Per-school split matches exactly: Athenian 16,252 (21 codes), CFP 1,634 (14 codes), Crestwell 334 (4 codes).

MECHANISM (end-to-end, verified in code + data):
1) SEED POLLUTION: supabase/seeds/dim_standard.csv ships substring-collision alias rows. Identifier c2a1b207 (canonical SS.6.W.3.1, "Analyze the cultural impact the ancient Phoenicians...") is attached to schoology codes SOC.6.SS.6.W.3.1 AND .3.10,.3.11,.3.12,.3.13,.3.14,.3.15,.3.16 (9 codes, one identifier) — the classic W.3.1-substring-matches-W.3.10..16 collision. Same signature for cbd1b207 (SS.8.A.3.1→A.3.10..15), ccd1b207 (SS.8.A.4.1→A.4.10..18), de61b207 (E.1.1→E.1.11..15), math codes (MA.1.GR.1, MA.6.AR.2, MA.912.AR.9.1). augment_standard_aliases.py:107-113 reproduces this exact "longest base that is a substring of the alias" logic.
2) FACT PIN: fact_student_submission.sql:223-231 LATERAL pins ORDER BY identifier LIMIT 1 (lexically smallest); the SQL comment lines 216-222 explicitly acknowledges the "CSV pollution" and that it deterministically pins the wrong (smallest) UUID.
3) CUBE COLLAPSE: cube_standard_summary.sql:46-51 ROLLUP groups on (school_id,item_id,strand_id,identifier) — NOT standard. Verified: Athenian item 7338323422 has 7 distinct benchmark codes (W.3.10-.16, Phoenicians/Roman Empire/Christianity — all different standards) collapsed into ONE cube row with total_standards=1 and a single pooled grade_average=0.7165 over 27 questions.
4) REPORT DISPLAY: cube_repository.py:879-884 get_standards_for_item (live via /api/v1/assessments/.../standards, assessment_service.py:151) fetches description via LATERAL(SELECT description WHERE identifier=a.identifier LIMIT 1), so identifier c2a1b207 renders the "Phoenicians" (SS.6.W.3.1) description with the pooled average — the wrong benchmark shown.

BENIGN EXPLANATIONS REFUTED WITH OWN QUERIES:
- Counting artifact/detector error: numbers reproduce exactly; all 44 codes have 2 DISTINCT descriptions and 43/44 have 2 DISTINCT CPALMS Preview IDs — genuinely different standards, not duplicate rows.
- Legit parent/child (.a-.f sub-parts): the .a-.f groupings map to ONE identifier and are NOT in the ambiguous-44 (verified ELA.K.F.1.2 has 1 identifier); zero of the 44 ambiguous codes end in a letter; the finding correctly excludes them.
- Vintage relabel: all 23 wrong-pinned codes have 2 different descriptions AND 2 different CPALMS Preview IDs — real distinct benchmarks, not relabels.

CLASSIFICATION = source-data-corruption (with a pipeline amplification component). The substring pollution originates in legacy's Spark ILIKE alias synthesis, baked into the shipped seed CSV — the wrong identifier+description was attached at source. Our pipeline faithfully mirrors it and then (a) pins the polluted identifier and (b) collapses distinct benchmarks in cube_standard_summary. PARTIAL MITIGATION EXISTS: the primary per-standard table get_standard_rollup_for_item (report_service.py:391) keys rows on schoology_standard and sources grades via cqso_by_code (exact code match), so the main SDD/QRA standards table shows the correct per-code grade and does NOT pool — the authors already defended this surface (GAI-8 lineage). But (1) the identifier-grain get_standards_for_item surface still shows wrong description + pooled average, and (2) cube_standard_summary.total_standards genuinely undercounts. Real, downstream-visible defect — needs fixing at the seed (purge polluted alias rows / exact-match alias synthesis via refresh_standards.py) then rebuild fact identifier + cubes. Evidence CSV: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/SCG-1.csv

Identifier-collapse examples: c2a1b207 carries 8 W.3.x codes; cbd1b207 carries 6 SS.8.A.3.x codes; ccd1b207 carries 5 SS.8.A.4.x codes.
user_visible_symptom: In standards reports the results of questions tagged e.g. SS.6.W.3.14 are credited to the SS.6.W.3.1 identifier: wrong standard description is displayed, several distinct benchmarks collapse into one row of cube_standard_summary (pooled averages = wrong numbers per standard), and COUNT(DISTINCT identifier) undercounts total standards.
root_cause_hypothesis: SOURCE/seed defect: legacy notebook built dim_standard.csv alias rows via substring/ILIKE matching, so short codes (…W.3.1) substring-matched longer codes (…W.3.10-.16) and got the short code's identifier+description attached to the long codes. Our pipeline then deterministically pins the lexically-smallest identifier (fact_student_submission.sql LATERAL), which is the polluted one in 23/35 cases.
fix_direction: Purge the polluted alias rows from dim_standard (rows where the attached identifier's canonical code/standard_new contradicts the schoology_standard's trailing segment), regenerate from CASE/CPALMS via refresh_standards.py with exact-match alias synthesis, then rebuild fact identifier column + cubes. Validate with: no schoology_standard maps to >1 identifier unless legit parent/child (a-f sub-parts).

title: Standard/Strand Summary grade averages zero-poisoned: cqs→cqso ukey join silently misses 9-15% of questions and AVG(COALESCE(grade,0)) counts each miss as 0%
schools: Athenian Academy of Technology and the Arts
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED (critical). Independently confirmed with my own queries — did not reuse the reported SQL. Every load-bearing claim holds.

CORE MECHANISM (verified in code + DB):
- backend/app/repositories/cube_repository.py: get_school_strand_rollup (line ~1672) and get_school_standard_rollup (line ~1777) both build `qso_avg AS (SELECT ukey, AVG(grade_average) FROM cube_question_summary_overall GROUP BY ukey)`, then `LEFT JOIN qso_avg qa ON qa.ukey = sq.ukey`, then `AVG(COALESCE(qa.grade_average, 0))`. The buggy COALESCE-to-0 string appears TWICE on the current branch (audit/fix-data), so the bug is shipped. When the cqs ukey has no cqso match the join yields NULL and COALESCE turns it into a fake 0% score.
- Root cause confirmed at backend/app/transformations/04_dimensions_c/dim_question_data.sql:118-128: `ukey = uuid_8(school_id, session, assessment_type, item_name, subject, grade, question, correct_answer)`. Because it hashes the QUESTION TEXT and CORRECT_ANSWER, a single logical question_id that has variant question/answer text across its rows produces MULTIPLE ukeys; dim_question_data carries 2 ukeys/question. cube_question_summary and cube_question_summary_overall each collapse to a DIFFERENT representative ukey, so the read-time join drops the row.

DB EVIDENCE (my queries):
1) Distinct ukeys in cube_question_summary with NO matching cube_question_summary_overall row, per school: Athenian 3,160/24,334 (13.0%); CFP 617/6,678 (9.2%); Crestwell 549/3,585 (15.3%). Matches finding (3159/616/548) to within +1 each (trivial distinct-boundary diff).
2) Full replica of get_school_standard_rollup (school-wide, no slicer filters), shipped AVG(COALESCE(qa.grade_average,0)) vs correct AVG(qa.grade_average): standards with >=1 missing ukey = Athenian 445, CFP 228, Crestwell 140 → TOTAL 813 (EXACT match to affected_count:813). Understated by >5pp: Athenian 367, CFP 211, Crestwell 130 (finding said 369/213/132 — within rounding of the >5pp cutoff).
3) Every cited sample reproduced to the tenth: Athenian SOC.6.SS.6.G.1.3 18.06% vs 94.30% (38/47 ukeys missing), SS.6.G.2.2 11.73% vs 86.01%, SS.6.C.2.1 7.20% vs 75.60%, SOC.6.SS.6.W.2.2 19.14% vs 91.89%, SS.7.E.2.2 19.61% vs 88.00%, SS.6.W.2.8 10.72% vs 78.50%; Crestwell MA.3.NSO.1.1 18.85% vs 94.23%; Crestwell MA.3.NSO.1.4 correct_pct 302.41% (confirms the secondary grade_average>1 anomaly — 3 school-scoped cqso rows >1, max 3.024).
4) Item 7337889512 mechanism: 20 question-ukeys in cqs, 11 not in cqso (exact match to finding's "11/20 mismatch"); dim_question_data holds 2 distinct ukeys per question_id on that item.

SEVERITY: critical is correct — school-wide Standard Summary and Strand Summary pages (and XLSX exports) render hundreds of standards at 7-20% when students actually scored 75-94%, mis-bucketing them into 'Needs Attention' and deflating the at-target KPI.

FIX DIRECTION verified: commits d4c099c ('Standard Summary legacy parity') and 221bb10 ('Strand Summary legacy parity') exist in repo history (the standard-code-bridge / drop-COALESCE fix) but are UNMERGED — the buggy code still ships on main/audit-fix-data. Merging that work (after review) resolves it.

MINOR CAVEATS (do not affect the core finding): (a) the "1,502 missing ukeys on single-section assessments" sub-figure did not reproduce cleanly with my dim_section join (my join found 7,614 missing ukeys almost all mapping to <=1 section, so the mismatch is NOT a multi-section pooling artifact — consistent with the finding's thrust, just a different section source than the exact 1,502). (b) Crestwell grade_average>1 anomaly count = 3 school-scoped (finding said 4), but the max 3.02 matches exactly; it's a side-note.

evidence_file: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/RIM-2.csv (813 rows: school, schoology_standard, num_questions, missing_ukeys, shipped_pct, correct_pct, understated_pp).
refute_notes:
CONFIRMED, not refuted. Every benign explanation was tested and ruled out with my own queries.

MECHANISM VERIFIED IN SHIPPED CODE (main + audit/fix-data, cube_repository.py): get_school_strand_rollup (line 1656-1675) and get_school_standard_rollup (line 1755-1780) build qso_avg from cube_question_summary_overall keyed on ukey only, LEFT JOIN qso_avg qa ON qa.ukey=sq.ukey, then AVG(COALESCE(qa.grade_average,0)) — coercing every failed join to a fake 0%. title: latest_export dedupe window omits subject/grade/assessment_type — cross-bucket pruning erases whole grade-band copies and leaves the CFP 'Topic 8' 1-student/0% Higher-Ed phantom (Brock Smith) missing from his real class

repro_notes:
REPRODUCED with independent from-scratch queries. Did NOT trust reported SQL; rewrote the detector and hand-verified the mechanism.

1. Fleet-wide, ZERO students are missing from the fact for any item they took (302 stg item-student pairs = 302 fact item-student pairs; a global check found 0 students in staging absent from fact for their item). The window loses no student's responses.

2. All 42 (item,grade) buckets that exist in staging but not in fact belong to items that STILL EXIST in the fact under another grade (42/42) — zero items disappear. No assessment vanishes from reports.

3. The finding's "students_lost=305/306" is a COUNTING ARTIFACT: it measures at the (item,grade) grain, double-counting the SAME students who consolidated into the correct/newer bucket. 5. title: Per-section item_name variants (prefixes, word order, 'Chapter 16.1' vs 'Chapter 16 Part 1') break the same-name report merge keyed on subject_id
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED (true). Core claim fully verified with my own queries; affected_count = 4 Crestwell assessments confirmed.

MECHANISM VERIFIED (both DB + code):
1. Evidence SQL reproduced verbatim — 10 rows, exact item_ids/subject_ids match the finding.
2. Root cause in code: backend/app/transformations/03_dimensions_b/dim_item.sql:39-46 computes subject_id = uuid_6(school_id, subject, assessment_type, grade, session, item_name). item_name is a DIRECT hash input, so any character difference yields a different subject_id.
3. Merge keys on subject_id: backend/app/repositories/cube_repository.py:170-194 (get_canonical_kpis_for_item) pools sections only via item_id IN (SELECT item_id FROM dim_item WHERE subject_id = :subject_id). The assessment slicer lists one entry per subject_id (backend/app/repositories/dim_repository.py:51-60). Therefore variant item_names -> distinct subject_ids -> distinct dim_subject rows (I confirmed all 8 variant subject_ids are separate dim_subject slicer rows with identical subject/grade/type/session, differing ONLY by item_name) -> cannot merge, each becomes a separate report.

THE 4 SPLITS (each = same test, junk-renamed, disjoint students, different sections, same/adjacent dates, matching standards):
- G4 Math 'Multiply Fractions and Whole Numbers': 8206618250 'Chapter 11 Test:...' Sec A (15 stu) vs 8206619117 'Chapter 11 ...' Sec B (15). Both 11 q, identical stds MA.4.AR.1.1/AR.1.3/FR.2.4.
- G2 Math 'Money': 8230928452 'Chapter 11 Test: Money' Sec A (17) vs 7928772123 'Chapter 11 Test: Money (overriding)' Sec B (15). Std MA.2.M.2.2.
- GK Reading 'Happy Healthy Me': 8226436104 'Module 4 Assessment:...' Sec A (13) vs 8226436129/8226431238 'Module Assessment:...' Sec B(12)/C(14). Stds ELA.K.F.1.3.c/F.1.4/R.1.1/R.2.2.
- GK Reading 'I Can Do It!': 8261135064 'Module 5 Assessment:...' Sec A (13) vs 8261137849/8261130285 'Module Assessment:...' Sec B(10)/C(14). Stds ELA.K.F.1.3.c/F.1.4/R.1.1.
Student counts match the finding exactly.

CORRECTIONS/NUANCE:
- The finding's '9 in-chunk items' is a sweep-chunking artifact; the actual total is 10 item_ids across the 4 assessments (2+2+3+3). affected_count of 4 assessments is correct.
- I independently confirmed there are exactly 4 such splits at Crestwell (2 junk-strip: '(overriding)'/'Test:'; 2 module-number-drop: 'Module 4'->'Module', 'Module 5'->'Module') and NO others.
- CAUTION on detector design: matching on shared standard-set ALONE massively over-flags because sequential weekly tests (e.g. 'Wild West Week 1' vs 'Week 2', 'Communication Nation Week 1/2/Module Assessment') share standards but are genuinely DIFFERENT administrations on different dates and correctly merge their own sections. Those are NOT splits and must be excluded. The reliable discriminator is std-set match + core-topic match + IDENTICAL sequence position (only junk differs) + disjoint students across different sections.

BROADER PATTERN (beyond this Crestwell-scoped finding, confirms mechanism generalizes, matches the 'also reported as' notes): a precise junk-only detector (keep sequence numbers) found 13 cross-school split groups, incl. Athenian GK Math 'Chapter 16.1'/'Chapter 16.2'/'Chapter 16 Part 1', CFP G4 ELA 'Heroic Feats...' vs 'M4 W1 Heroic Feats...', CFP G3 ELA 'Module 8'/'Mod 8' Imagine!Invent!, Athenian 'Quiz #1'/'Quiz 1', and apostrophe-encoding 'Earth?s Resources'/'Earth's Resources' (CFP G1 Science). These are real but outside the 4-count Crestwell finding.

SEVERITY: agree with 'high' — teachers see the same test twice in the slicer (incl. visible '(overriding)' junk label), each report covering only part of the cohort; grade-level and per-section comparisons fragment. Not 'critical' because per-half numbers within each split report are internally correct.

refute_notes:
VERIFIED REAL, but MISCLASSIFIED as a pipeline bug — the true root cause is source-side, and our pipeline faithfully mirrors legacy.

Evidence SQL reproduces exactly (10 rows across 4 assessment families). Adversarial testing established:

1. SPLIT ORIGINATES IN SOURCE, NOT OUR PIPELINE. The variant item_names are already distinct at the earliest transformation layer (stg_student_submission), which ingests item_name verbatim via `NULLIF(TRIM(rss.item_name),'')` with zero canonicalization. The differences — "Module 4 Assessment:" vs "Module Assessment:", "Chapter 11 Test:" vs "Chapter 11", "(overriding)" suffix — are teacher-entered Schoology labels present in the raw export. Confirmed at fact grain: each variant is a distinct section_nid with its own teacher, date, and even question count (e.g. Happy Healthy Me Sec B has 18 questions, Sec A/C have 20).

2. subject_id = uuid_6(school_id, subject, assessment_type, grade, session, item_name). item_name is a HASH INPUT, so any character difference deterministically yields a different subject_id. The merge-same-name feature (b480e26) keys on subject_id, so it cannot unify differently-named sections. This is documented, intentional behavior.

3. LEGACY DOES THE IDENTICAL THING. The decoded legacy PBIX spec (data/_pbix_extract/40_schoology_py_spec.md:479) computes `Subject_ID = generate_uuid_6(School_ID, Subject, Assessment_type, Grade, Session, Item_Name)` — same formula, item_name as hash input. The legacy spec contains NO item_name normalization anywhere (only HTML-tag stripping on the Question BODY, CR/LF cleanup on standards, a co-teacher-name UDF). Therefore legacy ALSO splits these exact items into separate subjects and separate reports. Our output is a faithful mirror; the "same test twice in the slicer" and visible "(overriding)" symptom exist in legacy too — this is not a regression we introduced. Crestwell's item_filter_expression is empty, so legacy does not strip "(overriding)" either.

4. THE MERGE FEATURE WORKS CORRECTLY. Proof: Happy Healthy Me Sections B and C both carry the identical name "Module Assessment: Happy Healthy Me", share one subject_id (9d78df...), and DO merge into one report. Only Section A ("Module 4 Assessment...") splits off — solely because its source name differs by "4 ". The detector's mechanism claim is correct; the pipeline is behaving exactly as designed and as legacy behaves.

WHY NOT refuted=true: the user-visible symptom is genuinely real and worth fixing (fragmented cohorts, junk "(overriding)" label visible, grade-level comparisons split). I cannot demonstrate it is benign-by-design because it is a real data-quality defect. But I refute the implied classification: this is source-data-corruption we mirror from legacy, NOT a defect our transformation causes. The finding's own root_cause_hypothesis ("Source-side... renamed inconsistently by teachers") already concedes this; only the category label ("split-assessment", high, implying our bug) is wrong. The proposed fix (per-tenant item_name canonicalization overrides) is a legitimate PRODUCT ENHANCEMENT that would deliberately DEVIATE from legacy parity, not a bug fix restoring correct behavior — it should be treated and reviewed as such. title: Impossible per-question points: points_received > points_possible on 74 fact rows (extremes 66/1 and 11/1, incl. healed-provenance mis-scaled values)
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED core claim exactly. Independent queries confirm 74 fact rows with points_received > points_possible across 12 items / 38 students. CORRECTIONS TO FINDING:
1. CODE CLAIM IS WRONG. Finding says per-student report (student_repository.py:106-126) "does not filter poss>0." It DOES — _FACT_SCOPE_SQL at backend/app/repositories/student_repository.py:49 applies 'f.points_possible IS NOT NULL AND f.points_possible > 0' inside the fd CTE (line 102) that feeds per_sg/per_student. Verified live: a Spelling Test student (Athena Gavallas, item 7699024272) computes 100.0% through the real report grain (10/10), NOT 120%. The 120% appears only WITHOUT the filter (12/10). So pattern (a) poss=0 does NOT reach the per-student report.
2. The '120% / 12.00/10.00' number is REAL but for cube_user_summary (total_score_by_question / total_possible_point_by_question = 12.00/10.00 for those students), NOT the per-student report. The cube path does include poss=0 points; the per-student repo does not. Leak is real, mis-attributed to the wrong code path.
3. '69 cube user-item rows exceed 100% overall' does NOT reproduce. by_question over-100% = 1001 rows across the same 12 items (Athenian 287 / CFP 146 / Crestwell 568 distinct student-item-questions); by_overall = 122 distinct student-items / 7 items; by_item = 68,968 (a SEPARATE cube-grain aggregation artifact, e.g. 540/20 on unrelated items like 8161441039 'Mid-Year Test' — not this defect). No metric yields exactly 69. Qualitative downstream impact (students show >100%) is confirmed.
4. 'file_name=empty' is imprecise: the 66/11 rows have file_name NULL (not ''), and ALL rows on that healed item are NULL, so NULL provenance is not unique to the anomalous rows.
5. poss=0 count is 34, not the finding's stated 35.

Pattern (b) genuinely inflates the per-student report: Alexandra Garcia = 390% on item 8007341041 (78 recv / 20 poss at report grain). Severity high is justified. Empty file_name is universal (100% of all 1.65M fact rows across all 3 schools), so it is not a healing/synthesis marker. No transformation scales points: stg_student_submission.sql:60-61 and fact_student_submission.sql:122-123/320-321 copy points_received/points_possible verbatim (no arithmetic/regex/scaling anywhere staging->fact->cube).

Source-origin proof: All 74/74 anomalous fact rows have an identical (school,item,question,pr,pp) row in stg_student_submission. repro_notes:

ROOT-CAUSE MECHANISM (verified, and it is NOT uniform across the 5):
- Chapter 10 (7687719992) ALONE is the two-numbering-vintage case: the item exists under TWO assessment_type labels in dim_question_data — "Assessments" (15 questions numbered 1-15) and "Lesson  Assessments" [double space] (20 questions numbered 1-20). dqd accumulated both vintages. Confirmed 14 (school,question_id,position) grains carry 2 different question_no values, ALL in this item; e.g. question_id 2109253463 = Q3 (Assessments) AND Q6 (Lesson Assessments), same identifier 3be72b67-.... This matches the finding's dqd claim exactly (14 grains, all item 7687719992, qid 2109253463 both Q3 and Q6).
- The other 4 items (8344562580, 8346388108, 7802005513, CFP 8018791881) are STRAIGHT NUMBER COLLISIONS within a single assessment_type/session: two genuinely different question_ids share one question_no (typically one row has a real correctly_answered value, the other blank/position-split). E.g. CFP 8018791881 Q2 = both "6,736×32" (qid 2190300723) and "BEST estimate for 811÷37" (qid 2190300725) — clearly two different questions numbered 2. So the finding's single root-cause hypothesis (vintage accumulation) fully explains only Chapter 10; the other 4 are source-level number collisions, which the finding's fix_direction already acknowledges ("for the 4 collision items verify against the newest Question-Data export").

CODE CLAIM VERIFIED: backend/app/repositories/cube_repository.py get_questions_overall_for_item(): qs_meta CTE (~line 651) is `SELECT DISTINCT ON (question_no) ... FROM cube_question_summary ... ORDER BY question_no, position_number` — for a colliding question_no it keeps ONE representative row and silently drops the other question's metadata/text. qs_num CTE (~line 663) does `SUM(total_score)/SUM(total_possible_point) ... GROUP BY question_no`, blending both questions' points into one grade for that question_no. So in merged multi-section / subject-keyed reports one of the two questions is dropped from display and its stats blend into the survivor — exactly the reported symptom.

SEVERITY: high (teachers see two different same-numbered rows, or in merged reports one question is dropped/blended — wrong/missing data, but not silently-wrong headline KPIs everywhere).

The user-visible symptom is real: the report reader cube_repository.py get_questions_overall_for_item uses qs_meta = SELECT DISTINCT ON (question_no) ... which keeps exactly ONE question per question_no and silently drops the other (I simulated it directly: FAST ELA Q7 keeps 'In Passage 2, how does the timeline...' and drops 'Read the sentence from Passage 2').

(2) true_collision_same_number — 4 items (3 Athenian, 1 CFP): within ONE section+assessment_type, one question_no maps to two genuinely different questions, and in MOST slots BOTH question_ids have real scored students (7802005513 Q4: 7+7; 8018791881 Q2: 14+14 with distinct math prompts '6,736×32' vs '811÷37'; only FAST-ELA Q7 has one side with 0 scored).
