title: submission_grade is raw points (not percent) and multi-attempt/partial exports leave row-sums matching neither the official grade nor any percent (1,075 attempts; one student's grade exceeds points held)
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED — every core number matches with my own independently-written queries (I did not reuse the reported SQL structure but arrived at the same aggregation grain).

CLAIM 1 (submission_grade is raw points, not a percent): CONFIRMED. Building per-question dedup (max points_received/possible per school,user,item,submission,question) then summing per attempt: submission_grade equals the row-sum of raw points earned for 68,534/69,623 attempts = 98.44% (finding: ~98%). Per school match_points = Athenian 52,158 / CFP 10,660 / Crestwell 5,716 — EXACT match to finding. Only 42+18+7 match a percent reading. Global sg range = 0.00-96.00 (finding: 0-96). submission_grade is NOT a percent.

CLAIM 2 (1,078 match neither; 1,075 in multi-attempt): CONFIRMED EXACTLY. match_neither total = 1,078 (Ath 226 / CFP 697 / Crestwell 155). Of those, 1,075 belong to multi-attempt user-items, 3 single-attempt. sg>row-sum globally = 1,089; sg>row-possible globally = 753 — both EXACT to finding (proves questions provably missing from an attempt's rows).

CLAIM 3 (affected_count 1,020 = distinct multi-attempt user-items): CONFIRMED. count of distinct (school,user,item) with n_attempts>1 = exactly 1,020. This is the population where per-attempt / attempt-agnostic reads are unreliable.

CLAIM 4 (latest-per-question merge reconciles 836/1,020): CONFIRMED. DISTINCT ON (school,user,item,question) ORDER BY submission DESC, sum recv, compare to max(submission_grade): 836 reconcile, 184 residual. Finding says 836/1,020 (exact) but states residual '170' — that conflicts with its own arithmetic (1020-836=184); my 184 is internally consistent. Minor, does not affect conclusion.

SAMPLES: all confirmed. item 7628347421 'HW 12/10 Spiral Review' = 29 attempts sg>rowsum (exact). The 8 cited multi-attempt items (8165582446 Chapter 10 Test =22, 8016821134 US History Quiz 2 =19, 8087335627 =18, 8087341078 =17, 8352495237 =17, 8193578592 =16, 8352493441 =16, 8117832042 =15) all match their attempt counts. 'Unit 9 Lesson 3 Braincheck' (Athenian user 127397209, item 7635138239): sg=4 but rows hold only 2 questions / 2 points possible — grade exceeds points available in held rows (truncated submission). Crestwell user 134955438 item 8235931624 carries two submission_grade values {15,18} inside one attempt (submission=1) — CONFIRMED, though its item_name is 'Chapter 12 Test: Relate Fractions and Decimals' not 'Chapter 10 Test' as the finding description said (minor label typo in finding).

PIPELINE-LOGIC (cube_question_summary.sql:98-116): CONFIRMED. Inner per_student_question CTE (lines 108-116) includes `submission` in GROUP BY, so the outer SUM(points_received)/SUM(points_possible) at lines 102-105 counts each attempt as a separate data point. A retaker who attempts a question multiple times contributes multiple rows to the question SUM/SUM average, weighting retakers by their attempt count (legacy PySpark parity, per code comment). This is intentional and documented.

CONCLUSION: Finding stands. submission_grade must never be treated as a percent; every score read should standardize on latest-attempt-per-(question,position) dedupe (submission DESC). Per-attempt or attempt-agnostic aggregation is unreliable for the 1,020 multi-attempt student-assessments. Severity medium is appropriate: this is a latent correctness risk for retake students, not a currently-visible wrong number in the sound (latest-attempt-dedup) report path, but any query touching submission_grade or partial attempt rows would produce wrong per-assessment scores.

Evidence CSV (1,078 match-neither attempt rows with school/user/item/name/submission/n_attempts/rowsums/sg/classification/flag) at: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mac-Desktop-PS-P-gains-platform/4daa84c4-b49c-4f9a-a5e9-8e3780b8e47d/scratchpad/audit/score-sanity-4.csv

title: fact points_possible disagrees with dim_question_data.total_points on 47 question-positions (one question varies across students)
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED (core claim holds; count corrected 47->43). WHAT I DID: Wrote my own deterministic set-based queries (did not trust the reported SQL). Fact grain for points_possible = numeric(10,4); dim_question_data.total_points = text; join on (school_id, question_id, position_number) — verified question_id+position maps to exactly one item in fact, so grain is sound.

CATEGORY 1 — INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT FACT (fully confirmed, exactly as claimed): 3 question-positions, all belonging to ONE question: Athenian item 7337971335 'Chapter 6 Perimeter and Area', question_id 2018660747, positions 1/2/3. 22 students per position: 20 scored on points_possible=1.0, 2 on points_possible=3.0 (mixed/partial re-export). CATEGORY 2 — MISSING QD DENOMINATOR: 24 question-positions where the fact has a real (non-null) points_possible but dim_question_data has NO row at all. All 24 are Athenian. (My raw no-qd-row count was 41, but 17 of those — 9 CFP + Crestwell 'n/a'-position rows + others — have NULL fact points_possible, so they cannot disagree with anything; excluding them gives the same 24 the reported query found. Confirmed the reported query's max()+IS NOT NULL filter correctly drops the NULL-denominator rows.) On these 24, cube_user_summary derives 0 possible-points (NULL total_points -> contributes 0 to sums), understating the denominator.

CATEGORY 3 — TRUE FACT-vs-QD MISMATCH: 16 (not 23), using a deterministic set-based test (flag only when the fact value is NOWHERE in dim_question_data's total_points set for that key). Breakdown: 2 Athenian, 2 CFP, 12 Crestwell (matches finding's 'mostly Crestwell'). Confirmed samples: Athenian 7702559165 'Chapter 16' q2112892373 pos3 fact 3 vs qd 1; CFP 8341726127 'Topic 8 Industrial Revolution' q2265107056 fact 0 vs qd 1; CFP 8369994919 'Topic 9 Nationalism' q2271800941 pos3 fact 4 vs qd 1; Crestwell 8007313247 'Use Place Value' q2187635400 pos1-3 fact 3 vs qd 1; Crestwell 8089974282 'Once Upon a Time' q2205490801 fact 5 vs qd 1; Crestwell 8117881781 'Chapter 7 Test' fact 3-4 vs qd 1.

WHY 16 NOT 23 — the reported evidence_sql is NON-DETERMINISTIC: its qd CTE uses DISTINCT ON (school_id,question_id,position_number) ORDER BY 1,2,3 with NO tiebreaker on total_points. dim_question_data has 14 question-positions with multiple distinct total_points values (e.g. 'Use Place Value' pos2/3/6 hold BOTH 1.0 and 6.0), so DISTINCT ON arbitrarily picks one and flags a spurious mismatch even when a matching value exists. Confirmed false positive: 'Come to Your Senses' weekly assessments — cited as fact 2 vs qd 5 — actually match perfectly under set comparison (fact and qd are identical). Rerunning the exact reported SQL gave 26 mismatch + 24 missing (not the finding's 23+24), confirming the instability.

CODE CLAIM VERIFIED: cube_user_summary.sql:53 derives total_points_num = NULLIF(qd.total_points,'')::numeric from dim_question_data (fact_join_qd CTE), feeding ALL possible-point aggregates (base total_possible_point line 200, by-question, by-item, by-standard). cube_question_summary.sql:102-106 computes its percentage denominator from SUM(points_possible) = the FACT column (only attaches qd.total_points as display metadata at line 276). So the two read paths genuinely use different denominators on these questions -> teacher-visible percentage vs displayed max-points can disagree.

BLAST RADIUS: small — ~12-13 distinct assessments (3 items missing qd, 9 items with true mismatch, 1 item internally inconsistent), matching the finding's '~20 affected assessments' order of magnitude (finding overcounted via false positives). SEVERITY: medium is right — teachers can see a max-points number in a question-detail table that differs from the percentage denominator on a handful of assessments, and one Crestwell/Athenian class average mixes incompatible point scales; low volume, latent-risk hygiene, root cause = source drift between Schoology's Question-Data and Submission-Summary exports plus one partial re-export. ROOT-CAUSE and FIX-DIRECTION in the finding are sound.

title: 5 CFP section_nids carry a DIFFERENT course's section label on some items (science items labeled as LA sections)

- 7891846801 'Unit 7 Benchmark: Working With Electricity': fact 'Sec 01 LA - A' vs canonical '05 SCI - A' (course 5154243536=05 Science), 19 stu.
- 7997342490 same test: 'Sec 01 LA - B' remnant (1 stu) vs canonical '05 SCI - B'; item also has correct 'Sec 05 SCI - B' rows (19 stu).
- 7891794271 'Unit 8 Test: Classifying Plants and Animals': 'Sec 04 LA - A' vs '03 SCI - B' (course 5154228700=03 Science), 17 stu.
- 7891742813 'Unit 8 Test: Forces and Motion': 'Sec 03 LA - A' vs '02 SCI - C' (course 5154218744=02 Science), 17 stu.

dim_item filing is CORRECT for all 5 (right subject_id/section_name/grade via dim_subject): the 4 science items are filed Science Grade 2/3/5 with SCI section_names; Topic 8 filed HS Algebra I / 'Regular 9–12' / 'HS ALG I - 7th'. So corruption is LABEL-ONLY in the derived layers, not in dim.

GRADE-BAND CONTRADICTION CONFIRMED: the 8362776921 US-HIST remnant carries fact grade='Higher-Ed' while dim_subject grade='Regular 9–12' — the known latest_export cross-band remnant signature (subject stays HS Algebra I, grade band diverges). The 4 science items keep correct fact subject=Science + correct grade.

- dim_question_data carries both correct and mislabeled section variants for the science items (subject/grade still correct there).
- cube_question_summary: 3 science items show correct subject/grade but WRONG section string ('Sec 0X LA'). - Overall cubes (cube_question_summary_overall_by_item) key on subject_id only and carry the correct Science subject_id, so aggregate rollups are unaffected.

title: Alias/parent-child standard codes resolving to the same identifier (AI.MA.912.* + MA.912.*, legacy MAFS composites) stored as separate fact rows — cube_standard_summary SUMs double-count points
schools: Athenian Academy of Technology and the Arts
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED (core mechanism confirmed exactly; scope and KPI-safety claims corrected/extended).

CORE CLAIM — CONFIRMED. I wrote my own queries (did not trust reported SQL). cube_standard_summary.sql (backend/app/transformations/09_cubes/cube_standard_summary.sql:26-51) does SUM(points_possible)/SUM(points_received) GROUP BY (school_id,item_id,strand_id,identifier) straight off fact_student_submission with NO dedup per (user,question,position). Fact grain includes `standard`, so 2+ codes mapping to one identifier get double/triple-summed. Cited example reproduced to the digit: item 7708642601, identifier 3ca92b67-8bad-44d5-bb62-d37ecb91f432 -> cube total_possible_point=180, total_score=164; deduped-to-(user,question,position) truth = 90/82 = precisely 2x. The two codes AI.MA.912.NSO.1.1 + MA.912.NSO.1.1 each carry exactly 90 fact rows. Reported OFFSET-1000/LIMIT-250 chunk reproduces exactly 12 items / 162 pairs.

Three code-family patterns all confirmed: course-alias (AI.MA.912.* + MA.912.*), parent/child (MA.7.AR.1 + MA.7.AR.1.1; MA.1.DP.1 + MA.1.DP.1.2 on the Chapter-16 Grade-1 items), MAFS sub-benchmark splits (MA.7.MAFS.7.RP.1.2.a/.b/.c), and a 6-way SS.6.W.3.10-.15 collapse.

CORRECTION 1 — SCOPE. affected_count:12 is a single-chunk sampling artifact. School-wide Athenian = 59 items / 110 cube cells. CFP ALSO affected (8 items / 16 cells) — finding scoped to Athenian only. Crestwell CLEAN (0). Corrected total affected_count = 67 items (126 cube cells) across 2 schools.

CORRECTION 2 — AGGREGATE INFLATION is 3.39x, not 2x, because many cells have 3-6 codes on one identifier (2 SS.6.W cells inflate 6x).

CORRECTION 3 (MOST IMPORTANT) — The finding's claim 'grade_average (percentage KPI) is UNAFFECTED' is FALSE in general. It holds ONLY for uniform, equal-multiplicity cells like the one cited. For 'mixed' cells (some questions double-tagged, others single) and cells where the two codes have different attempt-multiplicity, the ratio KPI IS corrupted: 72/126 cells shift >=0.5pp, 33 cells shift >=2pp, MAX percentage error = 15.93pp. Concrete: item 7801021169 identifier 3d0d2b67 (Algebra Gr8, AI.MA.912.F.2.1 + MA.912.F.2.1) cube 79.35% vs true 92.16% (-12.81pp); item 7632051430 (Math Gr7) 54.17% vs 62.12%. So severity is higher than 'latent hygiene': if any report surfaces cube_standard_summary grade_average for these standards, teachers see a materially wrong percentage NOW, not just wrong absolute totals.

SEVERITY: I'd raise from medium toward high given the percentage-KPI corruption on mixed cells — but agree the ABSOLUTE-total inflation is latent until a tile surfaces total_score/total_possible_point (yearly Standard Summary currently AVGs cqso by code, sidestepping it). Fix direction as reported is right: dedupe to one row per (user_uid,question_id,position_number,identifier) before SUM in cube_standard_summary.sql (or collapse alias/child rows at fact-build), and verify against KPI baselines since total_questions/total_standards must not move.

title: dim_section kept stale name 'Section A' after 2 Crestwell sections were renamed 'Section AB' (13 items show inconsistent section labels)
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED — finding STI-7 confirmed exactly. My own independent query (not the reported SQL) comparing dim_item.section_name vs dim_section.section_name for every (school_id,item_id,section_nid) that appears in fact_student_submission returns exactly 2 disagreeing sections, both Crestwell School (019eb11c-413c-7ed9-872e-0fe5e9a947b6): section_nid 7925706660 (8 items, Grade-5 Reading) and 7926805281 (5 items, Grade-5 Math). dim_section.section_name='Section A' for both; the 13 disagreeing items' dim_item.section_name='Section AB'. affected_count = 13, unchanged. The finding's cited sample item_ids all match my CSV exactly.

KEY QUERY (my version):
WITH isec AS (SELECT DISTINCT school_id,item_id,section_nid FROM fact_student_submission)
SELECT isec.section_nid, ds.section_name, di.section_name, count(*)
FROM isec JOIN dim_item di USING(school_id,item_id) JOIN dim_section ds USING(school_id,section_nid)
WHERE di.section_name IS DISTINCT FROM ds.section_name
GROUP BY 1,2,3;  -> exactly the 2 Crestwell rows (8+5=13).

CODE-CLAIM VERIFIED: The finding cites get_assessment_meta preferring dim_section when its stored item_id matches, dim_item otherwise. Confirmed in backend/app/repositories/cube_repository.py:2069-2090 — sec_src LEFT JOINs dim_section ON ds.item_id=it.item_id, then COALESCE(NULLIF(ds.section_name,''), NULLIF(it.section_name,'')). dim_section stores exactly ONE item_id per section (7925711568 for Reading, 7998804078 for Math), so the join matches only those 2 items (resolving to 'Section A'); all other items fall back to dim_item's per-item value. Simulated: 16 items resolve to 'Section A' (only 2 via dim_section hit), 13 to 'Section AB'. After the DISTINCT string_agg (lines 2087-2090), a merged report header can render 'Section A, Section AB' comma-joined. The dashboard grid path (cube_repository.py:407-408 string_agg DISTINCT di.section_name) can also produce the comma-joined label purely from dim_item. Both symptoms confirmed as reachable.

NUANCE / correction to root-cause hypothesis: The finding frames this as 'dim_section kept an older snapshot, dim_item captured the newer name.' My evidence shows the inconsistency actually lives WITHIN dim_item itself — for a single section_nid, 16 items carry 'Section A' and 13 carry 'Section AB' in dim_item. It traces to the SOURCE fact rows: fact_student_submission.section for section_nid 7925706660 holds three distinct values ('Sec Section A', 'Sec Section AB', 'Section AB') across different items, and for 7926805281 holds 'Sec Section A' and '' (empty). So this is source-side Schoology label drift per export (the Grade-5 Reading + Math classes were relabeled 'Section A'->'Section AB' mid-year, item-by-item), not a pure stale-dim_section artifact. dim_section happens to have picked the item whose fact rows said 'Sec Section A'. The proposed fix (latest-snapshot-wins per section_nid) would make dim_section internally consistent but would NOT by itself fix dim_item's per-item split — the durable fix must normalize the section label across all items of a section_nid at the dim_item/staging layer.

SEVERITY: agree LOW. section_name is a display label only; grade_average, total_students, and all report numbers derive from cubes keyed on subject_id/item_id independent of the label string, so no numeric impact — purely cosmetic 'Section A' vs 'Section AB' / 'Section A, Section AB' inconsistency across headers.

user_visible_symptom: Inconsistent section label ('Section A' vs 'Section AB') for the same class across different reports/headers.

fix_direction: Make the dim_section build latest-snapshot-wins per section_nid (or refresh its section_name from the newest dim_item row of that section).

title: file_name empty on 100% of fact rows — latest-export-wins prune inoperative (no present damage, latent re-ingest risk)
schools: Athenian Academy of Technology and the Arts
repro_notes:
REPRODUCED the two literal DB observations but REFUTED the finding's central claim and root cause. Core claim ("latest-export-wins prune is inoperative; the safety net cannot operate") is FALSE.

WHAT CHECKS OUT:
- Fact table file_name is 100% NULL/empty across all 3 schools: Athenian 1,294,185 rows / 0 with_file; CFP 241,653 / 0; Crestwell 111,150 / 0. Total 1,646,988 — exact match to finding.
- Damage check CLEAN: 0 conflicting-score cells at grain (school,user,item,question,position,COALESCE(sub_question,''),submission) HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT(points_received,points_possible))>1. Also 0 when adding answer_submission to the grain. Confirmed no present damage.

WHAT IS FALSE (verified against backend/app/transformations/07_facts/fact_student_submission.sql):
- The latest_export CTE (lines 130-175) parses export_ts from base.file_name (line 167), and base reads from stg_student_submission (line 125), NOT from the fact table. So the all-NULL file_name in the FACT table does NOT make the prune inoperative.
- stg_student_submission has file_name populated + parseable on 100% of student rows: Athenian 1,867,614; CFP 472,650; Crestwell 182,301 all parse to YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS.
- Re-running the CTE window on staging, the prune ACTIVELY FIRES: rows_pruned = Athenian 827,404; CFP 259,249; Crestwell 81,296 (total 1,167,949). This is exactly why the fact table (1.29M/242K/111K) is far smaller than staging student rows (1.87M/473K/182K).
- Root-cause hypothesis ("dev DB loaded from derived/parquet that drops the export filename; prune designed for raw CSV") is CONTRADICTED — this DB has full raw/staging with dated Schoology export filenames; the prune is precisely WHY there are 0 score conflicts, not because the source was pre-collapsed.

WHY fact.file_name is all-NULL: the final INSERT column list (lines 56-92) OMITS file_name. The column exists on the fact table but is never populated — a dropped passthrough column, not an inoperative prune.

THE ONE GENUINE (minor) point: the fact table's own file_name is unpopulated, so export provenance can't be audited from the fact table alone (must go to staging). That is hygiene/cosmetic (severity low). The 'no damage' is real but for the OPPOSITE reason the finding gives (prune fired hard; not pre-collapsed source). The separate 'partition omits grade' latent gap is a different, already-documented issue and is not what this finding measured.

CORRECTED COUNT: reported affected_count 1,646,988 (all fact rows) mischaracterizes the situation. The operative, accurate number is 1,167,949 = rows the latest_export prune actually removed (827,404+259,249+81,296), which proves the prune OPERATES rather than being inoperative.

Damage check: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT school_id,user_uid,item_id,question_id,position_number,COALESCE(sub_question,''),submission FROM fact_student_submission GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT (points_received,points_possible))>1) x; -- 0

root_cause_hypothesis: This dev DB was loaded from derived/parquet data that drops the source export filename; the prune was designed around raw CSV ingest where file_name embeds the export timestamp.
fix_direction: Have the parquet/derived loaders preserve (or synthesize) the export timestamp into file_name, or add a guard in the fact build that WARNs when 100% of rows lack export_ts; also remember the known open latest_export gap (partition omits grade) documented in memory for when file_name-bearing ingest resumes.
